Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 26-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025 / JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: HUM 3021/HUM_3021 ENGINEERING ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT  
  (SPL: ELECTRONICS & COMMUNICATION ENGINEERING)  
  ENGINEERING ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT [HUM 3021]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
Missing data may be suitably assumed.  
Interest factor table is provided for others use formula.  
Formula book is attached with the paper.  
  
1A)               Mr. Ramesh initiated a structured investment plan on March 1, 2020, by depositing a fixed amount (4)  
  each month into a savings account that earns 10% nominal interest compounded monthly. His  
  objective was to build long-term savings while maintaining liquidity through regular quarterly  
  withdrawals. Each monthly deposit amounts to ₹2,00,000. These deposits were made on the 1 st of  
  every month from March 1, 2020 to October 1, 2025.  
  Simultaneously, the account provided quarterly withdrawals to meet short-term financial needs. The  
  first withdrawal of ₹5,00,000 occurred on July 1, 2020, and similar withdrawals continued every  
  three months until October 1, 2025. Calculate the amount available in the account as of October 1,  
  2025, after the deposit and withdrawal on that day.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               Alex is considering buying property that comprises a plot of land and a shop. The land is predicted (3)  
  to increase in value by ₹30,00,000 over five years and shop has no salvage value. The shop can be  
  rented out immediately for a net annual revenue of ₹3,50,000. Annual maintenance expenditures  
  are estimated to start at ₹50,000 in the second year and grow by 2,000 annually. If Alex wants a  
  20% return on his investment, how much can he pay for this property now?  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
1C)            Ravi is planning for his retirement. He has 10 more years until retirement. He decides to deposit       (3)  
  ₹12,000 at the end of the first year and will decrease the amount by ₹700 each year for the next 7  
  years. If the savings account offers an interest rate of 10% per annum, what will be the total  
  accumulated amount at the time of retirement?  
  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)     On 31 st December 2011, two machines originally purchased on 1st January 2008 had to be                (4)  
  discarded due to irreparable damage. At the time of purchase, the first machine cost was ₹15,000  
  and had an estimated useful life of 10 years, while the second machine cost was ₹12,000 with an  
  estimated life of 8 years. Both machines were sold for ₹5,000 each at the time of disposal. The task  
  is to determine the resulting capital gain or sunk cost under two depreciation approaches: the  
  Declining Balance Method (rate of depreciation is 10%) and the Double Declining Balance Method  
  for the two machines.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)     An Indian consulting firm is considering acquiring an all-electric car for its employees to travel to (3)  
  client sites. The base price of the car is ₹32,78,000, but the company is eligible for a government  
  subsidy of ₹7,50,000, which reduces the effective purchase cost. The firm is evaluating two options:  
  it can lease the car by paying ₹4,20,000 per year at the end of each year, along with an initial cost  
  of ₹2,50,000, or it can purchase the car and a home charging station. The home charging system  
  costs ₹2,20,000. The company expects that after 3 years, the car and charging station can be sold  
  for 40% of the car's base price. Using an interest rate of 10% per year, should the company  
  purchase or lease the vehicle? Use annual worth approach.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2C)   E&T Construction Company is bidding to build a bridge across a river on a major highway connecting      (3)  
  two metropolitan cities in the coastal area. Therefore, severe cyclones are expected to hit the project  
  area every six years, causing structural damage, adding on to the costs. According to the tender, the  
  company must construct and maintain the bridge over the years forever. Determine the total amount for  
  which the company must bid now (assume interest rate of 8%).  
  The project engineers have estimated the following costs:  
  
  
  Page #2

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3A)    A company is starting pilot plant operations for a new process it has developed. One optional piece of   (2)  
  equipment that can be purchased is a heat exchanger unit. The company finds that a similar unit is  
  available now for ₹26.50 lakhs. This unit can also be used later in other company projects. It is  
  estimated that the heat exchanger will have a resale value of ₹30.74 lakhs at the end of 8 years. The  
  high resale value is mainly because the current purchase price is considered a rare bargain. If the  
  company expects a 10% annual rate of return, what annual benefit (in ₹) must the equipment generate  
  to make the purchase worthwhile?  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3B)   A manufacturing firm is evaluating two production lines - the existing one (A) and a proposed new one (B). (4)  
  
  
  Page #3

The contractor's minimum acceptable rate of return (MARR) is 10% per year. Determine the number of miles  
  of ditch per year, the contractor would need to service for the two options to break even.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4A)   The operations manager at GreenFleet Logistics Pvt. Ltd. is reviewing whether to continue using an existing (4)  
  delivery vehicle or replace it with a newer model. The current vehicle, purchased six years ago, has a market  
  value of ₹3.5 lakhs now. If retained for another five years, its annual operation and maintenance (O&M) cost  
  will be ₹50,000 in the first year, increasing by ₹20,000 each year thereafter. The vehicle will have a salvage  
  value of ₹1.25 lakhs at the end of five more years.  
  Two replacement options are available:  
  
  
  Using the cashflow approach in replacement analysis, determine whether it is financially more viable to retain  
  the existing vehicle for another five years or replace it with either EcoDrive Model X or VoltRide Hybrid Z.  
  Assume the MARR of the company to be 10%.  
  
  
  Page #5

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)         The finance manager of Nova Textiles Ltd. is analyzing the company's short-term financial position   (4)  
  and efficiency for the year ending March 31, 2025. The following information is available:  
  Financial Information:  
  $$• Current Ratio = 2.5$$  
  $$• Quick Ratio = 1.5$$  
  • Inventory Turnover Ratio = 6 times (assuming closing inventory is equal to average inventory)  
  $$• Gross Profit Ratio = 25\% of Sales$$  
  $$• Net Sales = ₹18,00,000$$  
  
  
  Using the given information and applying ratio relationships, determine:  
  (a) The value of Inventory  
  (b) The value of Sundry Creditors  
  (c) The total value of Current Assets and Current Liabilities  
  The Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)         A company is evaluating two investment projects, Project A and Project B, under three possible       (2)  
  future economic conditions.  
  The possible cash inflows (₹ in lakhs) and their probability are as follows:  
  
  
  i) Calculate the Expected Monetary Value (EMV) for each project. Identify which project should be  
  selected based on the expected value criterion.  
  ii) Explain how the concept of Expected Value helps in managing project risk when future economic  
  conditions are uncertain.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)   Mithra Foods & Packaging, a small FMCG vendor in Coimbatore, is planning to buy a semi-automatic pouch           (4)  
  Page #6

filling machine to increase its packaging capacity. The machine costs ₹9,00,000 and is expected to last for 6  
  years. The annual production is estimated to be 30,000 pouches per year beginning from the first year  
  onwards. The annual operating and maintenance cost will be ₹90,000 for the first two years, and from the  
  third year onward, this cost will increase by ₹15,000 every year. In addition, an overhaul cost of ₹75,000 will  
  occur once every three years, including the last year of operation. The machine is expected to have a salvage  
  value of ₹90,000 at the end of its life. If the company's minimum attractive rate of return (MARR) is 10% per  
  year, determine the minimum selling price per pouch that Mithra Foods & Packaging should set to cover all  
  costs and have zero annual worth over the 6-year period.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5B)   Haixun Industrial Technologies (USA) Ltd., operating in Texas, is evaluating the purchase of a new automated         (4)  
  metal processing unit costing \$240,000. The equipment will incur annual operating costs of \$36,000 in the first  
  year, increasing by a gradient of \$11,000 per year due to rising maintenance and labor expenses. Its salvage value  
  declines by 20% each year from the initial purchase price for the first three years and from the fourth year onwards  
  the salvage value remains constant at \$50,000. The company's Minimum Attractive Rate of Return (MARR) is 12%  
  per year. Determine the economic service life of the machine and its subsequent minimum annual cost value.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)              Delta Traders had credit purchases of ₹12,00,000 during the year, with opening creditors of          (2)  
  ₹2,00,000 and closing creditors of ₹1,50,000. Calculate the Creditors Turnover Ratio and the  
  Average Payment Period (assuming 360 days in a year).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
